title: rate-limit degraded warning prescribes "Redis via @objectstack/service-cache", but that adapter refuses to start
body:
## Finding

Raised by the #24740 card thread (`session_01XyLjAesp3Fkx794wqMb4hK`) as an out-of-scope finding (class a). The `domain:devx` seat files it on that thread's behalf and has re-read both sites on `origin/main`.

**The warning gives a fix that does not work.** When no `cache` service is registered, the rate-limit store logs this warning (`packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/rate-limit-storage.ts:217-223`):

> a multi-node deployment needs a shared cache (Redis via @objectstack/service-cache) or each node enforces the limit independently (ADR-0069 D2)

**But that package rejects Redis at startup.** `CacheServicePlugin.init` (`packages/services/service-cache/src/cache-service-plugin.ts:80-86`) throws when `adapter === 'redis'`:

> Redis cache adapter is not yet implemented. Use adapter: "memory" or provide a custom ICacheService via ctx.registerService("cache", impl).

So an operator who follows the warning gets a boot failure. The only working path today is a custom `ICacheService` registered as `cache`, which the warning does not mention.

## Fix options (for triage)

- **(a) Change the warning:** point to the working path, a custom shared `ICacheService` registered as `cache`, and say that the bundled Redis adapter is not implemented yet. This is a small change in one file.
- **(b) Implement the Redis adapter** in `service-cache`. This is a feature, and the existing warning text becomes correct.

PR #25328 (#24740) already gives the documentation side the current truth: counters live in the kernel cache, which under `serve` is in-memory and per process. This finding covers only the runtime log line.
